description: Saves a screenshot of the open page (returned in the reply, so there is no file to read) and an ID image (one colour per object), and lists what is on screen and the named objects no look has seen, with their size and where they are: it catches a model at the wrong scale, out of view or never loaded, which a screenshot alone misses. Call it after game_open and after each visible change. `camera` views from another place for this picture only. A game drawn in passes (post-processing) is pictured as it drew its last frame, so state set since then shows after a step. `target` instead pictures one named object alone from the front, right, top and a three-quarter angle, framed to its size, in one picture: use it to check a model or procedural shape from every side. `sheet` instead pictures up to 9 moments in one labelled grid, each on a freshly reloaded page set with `state`, played with `steps` (as game_act) and `frames`: use it to compare stages, levels or views at once instead of a screenshot script. `zoom` instead pictures one part of the screen enlarged up to 4×, for detail too small to judge (an edge, text, a distant object).

target.description: The name of an object in the main scene.

zoom.description: [x, y, width, height] in the picture's pixels (as the boxes look lists).

name: game_look
